questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go outside of Europe and preferably to an English-speaking country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
University of Melbourne has an airport pickup service free of charge, but you must sign up for it around three days before you need it. Additionally, there is an orientation week which is quite nice, however it can be a bit hard to figure out which subjects to take in the beginning and which of them fit together in the timetable.
If you are in doubt about anything though, you can always go to Stop1 and they can help you.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Airport pickup and orientation week.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I stayed at Unilodge Lincoln House, however it was quite expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Unilodge Lincoln House was really close to campus and that was very nice and convenient.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Stop1

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the subjects I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you don’t get a subject, you really wanted to begin with, don’t worry. Be patient and wait, as a lot of people change classes in the beginning so a spot might open a few days later.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The assessment happens a lot more throughout the semester as opposed to UCPH where the final exam accounts for the entire grade. There are more small assignments as well as midterms.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Australia in the Wine World
Stem Cells in Development and Regeneration
Microbes, Infections and Responses
Performance, Potential and Development

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Australia in the Wine World was quite fun and with weekly wine tastings. Stem Cells in Development and Regeneration was very interesting and I really enjoyed it. Microbes, Infections and Responses was less of an immunology subject than I expected. It was mostly about different pathogens and their mechanisms. Performance, Potential and Development was quite easy going and only had two hours of teaching a week.

questions.answer: Housing was very expensive, but coffee is cheap ;)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were so many different societies.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Rent a car and drive to Wilsons Promontory National Park, it is absolutely stunning. We had six days off at some point and flew to Tasmania, I really recommend doing that as well. You can also drive on Great Ocean Road and combine it with a trip to the Grampians or take a short trip to Sydney. The possibilities are almost endless. A day trip to Phillip Island is also great.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, the culture is not that different from our own.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to people in your classes and join a society.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Look forward to it, you are going to have an amazing time and the time will fly by way too fast. Get started early on with the weekend trips or you won’t be able to do all of them.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It was all really great.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The time difference to the people back home was sometimes a challenge.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
